_metadata.description: Revisit triggers, their evaluation, and the operator-only promotion boundary.

requirements.title: A candidate must carry a machine-evaluable trigger
requirements.description: Creating or holding a node in `candidate` without a parseable revisit trigger is refused. The source documents state this as a prose rule with the word 'must' and nothing able to enforce it, which is the canonical shape of a capability requirement in disguise.

validation.notes: Reject a candidate node with an absent, empty, or unparseable trigger.
A node already in `candidate` cannot be updated in a way that removes its trigger.

requirements.title: Triggers are declared over facts, not free text
requirements.description: A trigger is a declared predicate over named facts with comparison operators and boolean composition. Free-text conditions are not accepted. The first version deliberately admits only operator-supplied and scenario-supplied facts; a more expressive language would become an unmaintainable rules engine.

validation.notes: Parse-and-evaluate table covering each operator, composition, unknown fact, and type mismatch.

requirements.title: Scheduled evaluation reaches trigger-met
requirements.description: An evaluation run scores every candidate's trigger against current facts and transitions the satisfied ones to `trigger-met`, recording which fact satisfied which clause. This is the first capability in the replaced surface that does something no document could.

validation.notes: A satisfied trigger transitions the node and records the satisfying facts; an unsatisfied one does not.
A full evaluation run over a seeded graph is idempotent — re-running changes nothing.

requirements.title: Unknown facts block rather than fire
requirements.description: A trigger referencing a fact with no current value evaluates to unknown, not false. The node stays in `candidate` and the run reports the missing fact. Treating unknown as false would silently keep candidates asleep forever, which is the failure this scenario exists to end.

validation.notes: A trigger over a missing fact yields unknown; the run output names the fact.

requirements.title: Promotion to active is operator-only
requirements.description: An agent-role caller may create a promotion proposal and may not transition a node to `active`. Only an operator-role call performs that transition. The source canon states 'agents never self-promote'; this makes it a permission rather than an instruction.

validation.notes: An agent-role transition to `active` is refused; the same call from an operator role succeeds.
A proposal survives across restarts and carries its proposing actor.

requirements.title: Triggers can be dry-run before saving
requirements.description: A caller can evaluate a candidate trigger against current facts without saving it, so an author learns that a trigger is unsatisfiable or already satisfied at write time rather than a quarter later.

validation.notes: Dry-run returns the verdict and the facts consulted, and writes nothing.

requirements.title: A fact may carry a staleness window, and a stale fact is unknown
requirements.description: A fact may declare an observation date and a staleness window. Past that window it evaluates as unknown rather than as its last value, so a trigger resting on an expired observation reports the gap instead of firing on an old number. This is what lets market benchmarks live in the fact registry: a competitor comp is an observation with a dimension-derived window — pricing 90d, retention and activation 180d, channel-cac 120d, everything else 365d — and the sweep that currently enqueues expired comps by hand becomes a scheduled evaluation. Windows are a property of the fact's dimension, not of the trigger that reads it, so two triggers over the same comp cannot disagree about whether it is current.

validation.notes: A fact past its window evaluates to unknown, not to false and not to its last value; the evaluation run names it as a gap with its observation date.
Window is derived from the fact's declared dimension; a fact with no dimension takes the default window rather than never expiring.
A trigger referencing a stale comp leaves its node in candidate and reports the stale fact, matching GATE-004's unknown-blocks-rather-than-fires behaviour.
